To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the arterialisation of the thrombosed portal vein was performed successfully using a jump graft, which was anastomosed to the aorta and the portal vein.

the arterialisation of the thrombosed portal vein with an Aortoportal jump-graft can provide a viable portal blood flow and can be considered as a salvage procedure for patients with portal vein thromboses following liver resection.

1) arterialisation of the thrombosed portal vein with an interposition jump graft is feasible and can be used for patients with portal vein thromboses following major liver resection for liver malignancies; 2) this technique can be used for tumours with invasion of the portal vein; 3) the technique is feasible for patients with portal hypertension; and 4) the technique is also feasible for patients who have undergone a previous liver transplantation.

the development of an innovative and effective approach to the treatment of portal vein thromboses following extensive liver resection in patients with portal vein invasion by tumour.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

arterialisation of the thrombosed portal vein with an interposition graft is a feasible option for the salvage of a compromised liver remnant in patients with portal vein invasion from a hepatocellular carcinoma.
the use of aortic conduits for portal vein replacement in patients with FHCC is safe and effective, even in cases with a compromised portal vein.
arterialisation of the porto-systemic venous shunt is a safe, feasible and effective option to restore the porto-caval blood flow in patients with portal vein thromboses following liver resection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of an extensive liver resected for a tumour with compromised portal vein, arterialisation of the vein with an aorta-portal jump graft can be a feasible and safe alternative for the treatment of portal vein thromboses, which may be encountered postoperatively.
arterialisation of the compromised portal vein with an interposition aortoportal graft can provide a safe and effective option in selected patients with FHCC.

aggressive surgical resection for FHCCC is still a viable option and that arterialisation of the porto-systemic collaterals is a safe procedure that should be performed in cases of portal vein thromboses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the arterialisation of a portal vein is a feasible and safe option in selected patients with a compromised portal vein, who are not suitable for a conventional portal venous reconstruction.
, even in the presence of portal vein invasion, aggressive curative surgery can still be considered, with a good chance of long-term survival.

arterialisation of the porto-systemic collaterals with an aortobepatic shunt can be a life-saving measure in patients with portal vein thromboses following extensive liver resection, and can be a good option to bridge the patient to liver transplantation.
